newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SW Queensland gas price cut - Santos.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SW Queensland gas price cut - Santos.

text.p: Santos Ltd said on Wednesday that independent arbitrators had awarded a 7.5 percent cut in the price of gas sold by the South West Queensland Gas Producers (SWQGP) venture in one of its key South Australian contracts.

Santos said the decision affected about 10 percent of gas supplied from the Cooper Basin and, at current consumption levels, was expected to cut SWQGP profit after tax by about A$2 million in a full year.

"However, if volumes taken under this contract increase from the current rates of about 18 petajoules per annum as a result of the price reduction, the impact of the price reduction on revenue will be offset," the company said.
The maximum annual rate in the contract with the Natural Gas Authority of South Australia (NGASA), was 30 petajoules, it said. Santos has a 58.86 percent stake in the SWQGP venture.

Other partners are Exxon Corp's Delhi Petroleum Pty Ltd 23.2 percent, Boral Ltd unit Boral Energy Resources Ltd 16.5 percent, Australian Hydrocarbons Ltd 1.2 percent and Oil Co of Australia Ltd 0.24 percent.
Santos said the SWQGP-NGASA contract was one of four contracts for supply of gas to the state, and it currently provided about one quarter of gas consumed there.
Most of the remaining gas consumed in South Australia (SA) was provided under contracts between the SA Cooper Basin Producers and the NGASA.

Santos said the price awarded by the arbitrators was 7.5 percent lower than that which previously applied under the contract, but was still greater than the prices paid under other SA Cooper Basin sales contracts which were not affected by the decision.
The new price was to be phased in from July 1, 1996, and fully applied from October 11, 1996, Santos said.
